answer: Each agent anchors to one island with a ferrous stake. An iron stake is driven into the ground; its magnetic grain pattern is hashed on-chain, a fingerprint no two stakes share. The stake releases one nectar proof daily, a time-locked token collectable only on-site, so the identity must return daily. A 500 POA bond backs each stake and random auditors re-scan them; a mismatch slashes the bond and burns the identity. Forging 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 island trips at $240 each, $240,000 total, plus 30 days of daily collection. Like a lighthouse keeper: one island, one key, no photocopies.
